facts.raw_span: involuntary movements of her left upper and lower limbs for more than 10 days
a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
slow response, reduced muscle strength, and positive tendon reflexes in her left limbs
Continuous, irregular involuntary movements of variable amplitude were observed in the left arm and leg
a blood glucose level of 8.59 mmol/L
a hemoglobin A1c of 7.43%
all other laboratory values within normal limits
Noncontrast CT of the head showed slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions
without evidence of acute infarction
high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia

concepts.why: Involuntary movements of the left upper and lower limbs, slow response, reduced muscle strength, and positive tendon reflexes are consistent with hemichorea.
The patient's history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus and elevated blood glucose level may be contributing to the development of chorea.
The high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia and increased density in the bilateral striatal regions are indicative of basal ganglia disease.
The patient's elevated blood glucose level and hemoglobin A1c are indicative of hyperglycemia.
The high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia and increased density in the bilateral striatal regions may be indicative of NBIA.
The patient's neurological examination findings and imaging results may be consistent with vascular parkinsonism.
The patient's history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus and neurological examination findings may be indicative of diabetic neuropathy.
The patient's involuntary movements and neurological examination findings may be consistent with Huntington's disease, although the age of onset is atypical.
